title: Prachinburi 2-Day Cafe Trip: Mountain Views + Old Town | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A 2-day, 1-night Prachinburi cafe itinerary in Thailand: start with mountain-view cafes around Noen Hom and Si Maha Phot, then walk the old town of Kabin Buri, Kum Market and the old railway station. Real spots, real hours.
keywords: Prachinburi cafe, mountain view cafe Prachinburi, Kabin Buri travel, Prachinburi itinerary, Myrrh Cafe
h1:
Mountain-View Cafes
+ Kabin Buri Old Town
intro: Prachinburi sits only about 2 hours' drive from Bangkok, yet it packs cafes set in nature, mountain views, and an old town along the railway into one trip. This plan runs 2 days and 1 night: day one works through the mountain-view cafes around Noen Hom and Si Maha Phot, and day two shifts gears for a slow walk through the old town of Kabin Buri. We checked that every place here is still open and listed real opening hours, because a lot of cafes around here only open on weekends.

blocks.html: Prachinburi isn't just Khao Yai on one side and the Abhaibhubejhr herbal town. Over the last few years, new cafes have spread across the Noen Hom area (the stretch before you climb up to Khao Yai) and Si Maha Phot district, which throw in views of Khao I-To and wide open fields for free. Over on the other side of the province, Kabin Buri district still holds the charm of an old town along the railway, with a century-old market to wander through. This plan ties those two moods together across 2 days.

Who it's for: people who drive their own car or rent one, like cafes, photos, and easygoing town strolls rather than serious hiking. Without your own car it gets tricky, because the cafes are spread out and public transport in the province is limited.

blocks.text: Day one: working through the mountain-view cafes around Noen Hom–Si Maha Phot

blocks.html: Day one focuses on the Prachinburi town–Si Maha Phot zone, the side closest to Khao Yai and Khao I-To. Most cafes around here get a mountain backdrop. One thing to know: some spots (like Myrrh) used to open only on weekends but are now open daily — still, always check the cafe's page before you set off.

items.note: Take the motorway/Route 304, around 2 hours. Grab your first coffee at a gas station along the way.

items.activity: Check in at Myrrh Cafe, Noen Hom
items.note: A white-toned cafe set in nature with a rooftop that gives you a 360-degree view and a clear look at Khao I-To. It's pet friendly. Open daily 9:30–18:00. The standout drinks are the Thai tea with coconut cream and the house blended drinks.
Drive into town for a proper meal — there's plenty of choice, from boat noodles to made-to-order shops in the town center, around 50–120 THB per plate.

items.activity: On to roaster cafe Compass Coffee Roasters (304)
items.note: On the Si Maha Phot side, right on Route 304. They roast their own beans — good for serious drip coffee fans, and an easy place to rest in the afternoon.

items.activity: Stop by Craftel Cafe, train theme
items.note: A train-themed cafe in Si Maha Phot with lots of photo corners — a good way to close out the late-afternoon light before heading to your hotel.

items.activity: Check in at your hotel in Prachinburi town
items.note: Staying in town makes it easy to find dinner and wander around. See accommodation options via the Top 10 link below.

blocks.title: A tip about opening hours
blocks.html: A lot of the cafes set in nature around here open only Friday–Sunday and on public holidays. Go on a weekday and you may find them closed. Open each cafe's Facebook page or Google Maps to check their days before you drive out, every single time.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Prachinburi trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

items.label: Day trips from Prachinburi
items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.text: Mountain-view and nature cafes people like to visit

blocks.html: If you have time to spare or want to adjust the plan yourself, these are the cafes on the Prachinburi–Si Maha Phot side with a natural setting and mountain views. We've ordered them by how well they fit the "mountain view + sit and relax" theme, not ranked which is better than which, because each one has a different vibe.

items.name: Myrrh Cafe
items.blurb: A white-toned cafe in a garden around Noen Hom. The highlight is the rooftop with a 360-degree view that puts Khao I-To right in front of you. There's a garden zone, an air-conditioned zone, and it's pet friendly. Standout drinks are the Thai tea with coconut cream and the house blended drinks.

items.name: Compass Coffee Roasters (304)
items.blurb: A real coffee-lover's spot in Si Maha Phot that roasts its own beans and leans on the coffee more than the photo scene. Good if you want to sip a quiet drip.

items.name: Craftel Cafe
items.blurb: A train-themed cafe in Si Maha Phot with stylish decor and plenty of photo corners — good for people who like cafes with a strong design.

items.name: BREW CAMP 304
items.blurb: An outdoor camp-style cafe with a relaxed, open-air feel in nature. Good for anyone who likes airy, uncrowded surroundings.

items.name: Into The Wild
items.blurb: A nature-themed cafe on the Prachantakham side, shady and green. A good stop along the way if you're looping out that direction.

items.name: The Forest Cafe1
items.blurb: A forest-concept cafe with plenty of trees and greenery. Good for anyone who wants to escape the bustle and sit somewhere quiet.

blocks.text: Day two: a slow walk through the old town of Kabin Buri

blocks.html: Day two trades the mountain-view cafes for an old town. Kabin Buri is on the other side of the province, about 40–50 minutes' drive from Prachinburi town. The draw is the old market quarter along the railway that was settled around a century ago — an easy place to wander, with old wooden buildings, Kum Market, and local cafes tucked in between.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Kabin Buri old town + Kum Market

items.activity: Check out, drive to Kabin Buri
items.note: About 40–50 minutes from Prachinburi town. Grab a light breakfast first if you like.

items.activity: Baan Mae Cafe, Mueang Kao subdistrict
items.note: A warm, woodwork-style cafe with a wooden boardwalk for a nature stroll and one-plate dishes made by the owner. Open Thursday–Tuesday 08:00–17:00, closed Wednesday.

items.activity: Walk the Kabin Buri old market quarter (Kum Market)
items.note: An old trading community by the railway station, with wooden buildings and traditional shops. Good for photos and finding local bites.
Find local food in the market quarter — noodles, rice with curry, or old-style sweets, all easy on the wallet.

items.activity: Stop by Kabin Buri Railway Station
items.note: The old station at the heart of town — walk around for the retro atmosphere and check the Eastern Line train schedule.

items.activity: Relax at Kabin Chaloem Rat Park
items.note: A public park in the middle of the district with a lotus pond and shady trees. A nice place to walk off lunch and rest before heading back.
Drive back to Bangkok in about 2.5 hours, or carry on to Sa Kaeo / Nakhon Nayok if you feel like it.

blocks.title: If you want to add a water view
blocks.html: With a spare half day, try driving out to Nuetbodindra Chinda Reservoir (Huai Samong), the largest reservoir in the province, with a long stretch of dam views — good for laying out a mat for a picnic and taking photos. But it's farther out, so allow extra driving time.

blocks.text: Cafes in Kabin Buri town worth a stop

blocks.html: If you want more cafe time on day two while you walk the town, Kabin Buri has several cute local spots. Most are small, owner-run places with an easygoing vibe.

items.name: Baan Mae Cafe
items.blurb: A woodwork-style cafe in Mueang Kao subdistrict with a wooden boardwalk for a nature stroll and homemade one-plate dishes. Open Thursday–Tuesday, closed Wednesday.

items.name: O'Mill
items.blurb: A family cafe behind Global House Kabin Buri, with DIY painting and bead-stringing activities on weekends. Open 09:00–20:00, closed Tuesday.

items.name: So Jaeng Slow Bar
items.blurb: A small slow bar in Kabin Buri, good for people who like coffee brewed unhurried, with a chilled-out feel.

items: Own car / rental — this plan spreads across several districts, so a car is by far the smoothest option. Public transport in the province is limited.
Check opening days — some nature cafes open only on weekends; Baan Mae Cafe closes Wednesday and O'Mill closes Tuesday. Always check the page first.
Best time to go — late rainy to early cool season (Nov–Feb) brings good weather, clear green mountain views, and rooftop cafes that aren't too hot.
Allow travel time — Prachinburi town to Kabin Buri is about 40–50 minutes, and Huai Samong needs even more on top of that.

faq.q: Where's the best mountain-view cafe in Prachinburi?
faq.a: The Noen Hom and Si Maha Phot side is the mountain-view cafe zone, since it's close to Khao I-To and Khao Yai. The spot people talk about for the view is Myrrh Cafe, which has a rooftop with a 360-degree view and is open daily 9:30–18:00.

faq.q: Do I need a car for a Prachinburi cafe trip?
faq.a: You should have your own car or a rental, because the cafes and sights are spread across several districts — Noen Hom, Si Maha Phot, and Kabin Buri. Public transport in the province is limited, so getting around without a car is tough.

faq.q: What is there to do in Kabin Buri old town?
faq.a: The highlight is the Kabin Buri old market quarter (Kum Market) by the railway station — an old trading community around a century old, with old wooden buildings and traditional shops, plus Kabin Buri Railway Station and Kabin Chaloem Rat Park, both easy to wander.

faq.q: How many days does this plan need?
faq.a: It's designed for 2 days and 1 night: day one works through the mountain-view cafes on the Prachinburi town–Si Maha Phot side, and day two walks the Kabin Buri old town. With only one day, you can do either half.

faq.q: When is the weather best in Prachinburi?
faq.a: Late rainy to early cool season, roughly November to February, when it's cool and pleasant, the mountain views are clear and green, and sitting at a rooftop or outdoor cafe isn't too hot.
